turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode), `etl`
(electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Every candidate below uses the
same MAPbI3 absorber in the same n-i-p (regular) architecture; they differ
only in the remaining columns. Each row is a device CONFIGURATION whose
efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently fabricated cells, so
it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_stack_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_stack_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning from the device physics

**What the training set says about winning stacks (all MAPbI₃, n‑i‑p):**

1. **A bilayer, doubly‑selective electron contact wins.** The highest entries all combine a compact oxide with a second, better‑matched electron‑selective layer: `TiO2-c | SnO2-np` (20.85), `TiO2-c | PCBM-60` (19.35, 16.4), `TiO2-c | C60` (17.2), `SnO2-c | PCBM-60` (17.3–18.0), `TiO2-c | BaSnO3-np` (18.9). Physically, the compact TiO₂ blocks holes/shunts while the SnO₂/fullerene overlayer lowers the conduction‑band offset, passivates surface Ti³⁺/oxygen‑vacancy traps and suppresses the UV‑photocatalytic and hysteresis behaviour of bare TiO₂ — i.e. it kills the dominant ETL/perovskite interface recombination channel.
2. **Bare single oxides, ZnO, CdS, nanowire and QD ETLs sit much lower** (ZnO chemical instability with MA⁺, deep‑trap CdS, poor pore filling of nw/QD scaffolds).
3. **On the hole side**, high performance requires either doped Spiro‑MeOTAD (with an inserted passivant/interlayer: PMMA, PbS‑QDs, graphene oxide → 16–18.6), a good conjugated polymer with matched IP (PTAA, PCDTBT‑type ≈ –5.1 to –5.3 eV → 15.5–19.4), or a fully doped evaporated organic p‑stack (TaTm/F6‑TCNNQ → 17.9). P3HT (IP –4.9 eV, no doping) and phthalocyanine/QD/inorganic HTLs cost 2–5 % absolute in V_OC·FF. HTL‑free carbon devices cluster at 5–13 %.
4. **Back contact**: Au (or Ag with a MoO₃ buffer) gives clean, non‑reactive, high‑work‑function extraction; bare Ag, Al, carbon, ITO/FTO counter‑electrodes lose FF.
5. **Process**: plain one/two‑step spin‑coating on glass/FTO(ITO) is the best‑behaved; flexible plastic, spray, doctor‑blade, slot‑die lose a few points through film quality.

**Applying this to the pool:**

- **c064** `TiO2-c | SnO2-np` + Spiro‑MeOTAD + Au — exactly the cascade‑ETL motif of the single best training device (20.85); rigid FTO glass, standard spin‑coating, ideal Au contact. Best expected.
- **c005** `TiO2-c | PCBM-60` + PCDTBT8 + MoO₃|Au — twin of the 19.35 % `PCDTBT1` device: fullerene‑passivated TiO₂, deep‑IP doped‑free polymer HTL, MoO₃ hole‑injection buffer under Au.
- **c017** C60;PhIm|C60 / TaTm / F6‑TCNNQ:TaTm, all co‑evaporated — the doped p‑i‑n‑type organic contacts give near‑ideal band alignment and pinhole‑free evaporated films (training analogue 17.9 %); only slight penalty for Ag instead of Au.
- **c043** `TiO2-c | TiO2-mp` + **DAHI interlayer** | Spiro‑MeOTAD + Au — the mesoporous benchmark plus an interfacial passivating layer at the perovskite/HTL junction, the same trick that lifted PMMA|Spiro to 18.0 and GO|Spiro to 16.2.
- **c080** `TiO2-c | MPMIC60` + Spiro + Ag — fullerene‑monolayer‑modified compact TiO₂, i.e. the same trap‑passivating/energy‑aligning cascade, with a conventional Spiro/Ag top stack (analogues 17.2–17.3 %).

Close runners‑up (just outside): c031 (SnO₂/SnO₂‑mp/TiO₂‑c + Spiro + Au), c073 (TiO₂|C60 + PTAA), c068 (SnO₂|TiO₂‑np + PTAA + Au|MoO₃), c045 (TiO₂‑nanofibre + PTAA).

Final: c064, c005, c017, c043, c080
